Field.Label: HTTPS Port:
Field.Description: 443 for UniFi OS consoles (UDM Pro etc), 8443 for self-hosted, 11443 for UniFi OS Server.

Field.Label: Site ID:
Field.Description: Usually 'default'. Multi-site setups will use the site short name.

Field.Label:
Network and Protect share a SINGLE key from the unified Integrations page: Settings → Control Plane → Integrations (or visit https://[controller-ip]/network/default/integrations/).
UniFi Access uses a SEPARATE token, generated inside the UniFi Access application itself (look for an API Token / Integrations menu within Access). The Access API runs on a different port (12445 by default) with Bearer authentication.
Access Port:
Field.Description: UniFi Access runs on its own port (default 12445), separate from the main HTTPS port.

Field.Label:
Required for endpoints not yet exposed by the official Integration API: • Network: PoE port mode toggle, client block/unblock, rich device stats • Drive (UNAS): all functionality
Use a LOCAL-ONLY admin account (Settings → Admins → Create New, tick 'Restrict to local access only'). Do NOT use a UI.com cloud account or one with MFA.
Test Connection:
Field.Title: Test All Configured APIs
Field.Description: Tests each enabled API independently. Watch the Indigo log for results.

Field.Label: Real-time events (motion, smart detect, doorbell, client connect/disconnect, port state, door unlock) arrive instantly via WebSockets and are NOT affected by these intervals. The intervals below only control how often slow-changing stats (CPU, memory, temperature, throughput, RPM) are refreshed.
Aggressive polling mode (30s):
Field.Description: Polls every 30 seconds. Only enable if WebSockets are unreliable on your controller.

Field.Label: Stats Poll Interval:
Field.Description: How often to refresh CPU, memory, temperature, throughput, fan RPM. Recommended: 5 min.

Field.Label: Sanity Re-Sync Interval:
Field.Description: Periodic full re-sync to catch any WebSocket messages that might have been dropped. Recommended: 15 min.

Field.Label: iPhones, Android phones, and Windows machines often use "private" (locally-administered, randomised) MAC addresses for privacy. These accumulate as visitors come and go. The purge can remove ones that haven't been seen for a while, both from Indigo and from UniFi itself. Run the "Purge Randomised Clients" action manually, or schedule it via an Indigo Time/Date trigger.
Purge after (hours):
Field.Description: Minimum hours since the client was last seen before it qualifies for purge. Default 24.

Field.Label: Skip if UniFi has a custom name:
Field.Description: Don't purge clients that have a custom name, hostname override, or user note set in UniFi.

Field.Label: Skip if has fixed IP or user group:
Field.Description: Don't purge clients with a fixed-IP reservation, user group assignment, or device-type override in UniFi.

Field.Label: Skip if an Indigo device exists:
Field.Description: Don't purge a client that's represented by an Indigo device (the user has explicitly added it).

Field.Label: Dry run (preview only):
Field.Description: When ticked, the purge action only logs what it WOULD remove without actually doing anything. Useful for testing the threshold.

Field.Label: When enabled, a new Indigo device is created automatically the moment UniFi reports a brand-new client connecting - no need to run "Create Unknown Clients" yourself. Respects the same "previously deleted" list as the manual discovery actions, so deleting a client device here won't bring it straight back.
Skip randomised/private MACs:
Field.Description: Phones and some other devices rotate a private MAC address for privacy - each rotation looks like a brand-new client to UniFi. Leave this ticked to avoid a constantly growing pile of devices for what's really the same phone. Named/fixed-IP clients are unaffected by this since they don't use a rotating MAC in the first place.

Field.Label: Save the controller config first, then click these to discover devices. New devices will be named with the prefix and suffix below — existing devices are not renamed.

Represents the secondary "package" lens some doorbell cameras have, alongside their main view. Mirrors its parent camera's full state structure (motion/detection/audio/connection/etc.) since it's the same underlying camera object - only the RTSP stream for this lens (enabled/disabled via the two actions below) is genuinely unique to this device.

Fetches this lens's current RTSP stream status, plus the parent camera's package-camera-related flags where legacy data is configured. Useful if this device doesn't seem to be finding a real package lens - doesn't require debug logging to be enabled.
Creates an Indigo device for each physical port on this switch. Only creates ports that don't already exist.

Fetches this device's full raw data and logs it in full. Useful for device types this plugin only partially recognises, or if a state looks wrong/blank/Unknown - doesn't require debug logging to be enabled.
Select the switch and port number for this device. Port states will update automatically.

• PoE Control: Device state shows PoE enabled/disabled • PoE Reboot: Off button uses UniFi power-cycle command (instant reboot) • Port Active: Device state shows port enabled/disabled (affects all traffic)
Fetches this port's full raw data (from its parent switch's port table) and logs it in full. Useful if a state looks wrong/blank/Unknown - doesn't require debug logging to be enabled.

List.Option: PoE Reboot (Off button power cycles port)

Field.Label: PoE control only works when client is connected via a PoE-capable wired port. If client is on WiFi or non-PoE port, control attempts will log a warning.
Fetches this client's full raw data and logs it in full. Useful if a state looks wrong/blank/Unknown - doesn't require debug logging to be enabled.

Only your own custom policies are listed (Ubiquiti's built-in/predefined ones aren't, since toggling those is rarely useful from automation). On/Off enables or disables the policy. If the list is empty or doesn't show a policy you expect, select the controller first, then reopen this menu.
Fetches this policy's full raw data and logs it in full. Useful if a state looks wrong/blank/Unknown - doesn't require debug logging to be enabled.
On/Off enables or disables the route. If the list is empty or doesn't show a route you expect, select the controller first, then reopen this menu.
Fetches this route's full raw data and logs it in full. Useful if a state looks wrong/blank/Unknown - doesn't require debug logging to be enabled.
On/Off enables or disables the rule. If the list is empty or doesn't show a rule you expect, select the controller first, then reopen this menu.
Fetches this rule's full raw data and logs it in full. Useful if a state looks wrong/blank/Unknown - doesn't require debug logging to be enabled.

On/Off enables or disables this SSID. Use the "Change WLAN Password" action to update its passphrase. If the list is empty or doesn't show an SSID you expect, select the controller first, then reopen this menu.
Fetches this WLAN's full raw data and logs it in full. Useful if a state looks wrong/blank/Unknown - doesn't require debug logging to be enabled. Passwords are never included in this dump.

EXPERIMENTAL - built without any Alarm Manager hardware to test against (see the plugin's ROADMAP.md on GitHub). On arms the system to this profile; Off disarms. Requires the Protect account configured for this controller to be a Super Admin with MFA disabled - no lesser role is known to work. If the profile list is empty, or arming/disarming fails, use "Dump Device Payload to Log" below and send the result to Durosity.

Dumps the full raw Protect bootstrap payload - deliberately not trimmed down to just what this plugin currently looks for, since that's exactly what's unconfirmed. Doesn't require debug logging to be enabled.

List.Option: Leave unlocked (stays open until explicitly locked)

Field.Label: This device represents a UniFi Access door lock. Lock always locks immediately. Unlock's behavior depends on the setting above: "Tap to unlock" re-locks automatically (within ~10s if the door is never opened, or once closed again if it is); "Leave unlocked" stays unlocked until Lock is pressed. Separate "Unlock Door (Momentary)" and "Unlock Door (Leave Unlocked)" actions are also available for Action Groups, regardless of this setting.
Fetches this door's full raw data and logs it in full. Useful if a state looks wrong/blank/Unknown - doesn't require debug logging to be enabled.

This device represents a UniFi Protect sensor (door, motion, temperature, etc.) "Primary State" controls what the device's on/off shows and means - Auto picks sensibly based on mount type (door/window/garage, leak, or general-purpose), or pin it explicitly if this sensor is used for something its mount type doesn't capture.
Fetches this sensor's full raw data and logs it in full. Useful if a state looks wrong/blank/Unknown - doesn't require debug logging to be enabled.
Pool Key:
Field.Description: Identifier for the pool (set automatically by discovery).

Field.Label: Each storage pool on the UNAS gets its own device for granular RAID, capacity, and rebuild monitoring.
Disk Key:
Field.Description: Identifier for the disk (set automatically by discovery).

Field.Label: Each physical disk in the UNAS gets its own device for temperature, health, and SMART-style monitoring.

Controls UNAS fan mode via Indigo's standard 4-speed control: speed 0 = Default (firmware auto-control), 1 = Quiet, 2 = Balance, 3 = Cooling. Use the "Set UNAS Fan Mode" action for direct mode selection by name.

The UNAS appliance is a separate device from the UDM Pro, with its own admin account and Integrations page.
Generate an API key from the UNAS web UI (Settings → Control Plane → Integrations on the UNAS itself). If your UNAS version doesn't yet support API keys, leave that field blank and use the local admin username/password instead.

The UNAS REST API for fan control is currently read-only on UniFi firmware (writes return HTTP 500). To actually change fan modes the plugin uses SSH to deploy a small fan control service to the UNAS. Enable SSH on the UNAS via Settings → Control Plane → Console and provide credentials below. Leave blank to disable fan control (monitoring still works).
Auto-redeploy after firmware updates:
Field.Description: Once a day, check whether the fan control script is still installed on the UNAS. If a UniFi OS update has wiped it, redeploy silently. Recommended.

Field.Label: Stats Poll Interval:
Field.Description: How often to refresh storage stats, fan RPM, CPU, memory. Recommended: 5 min.

Field.Label: Save the controller config first, then click these to create devices. The prefix/suffix below are applied to new device names.
